title: MSc Geo-information Science and Earth Observation at ITC, University of Twente
description: The largest dedicated geo-information faculty in the world. Partial ITC Excellence Scholarships and a 40 percent Early Bird fee waiver go to the strongest non-EU applicants.
deadline: Scholarship rounds close in the first months of the year; programme starts September

facts.label: Ranking
facts.value: University of Twente =223 in QS World University Rankings 2027; ITC is the largest postgraduate geo-information faculty worldwide, founded 1950

facts.label: Level and length
facts.value: MSc, two years, 120 ECTS, taught in English

facts.label: Tuition
facts.value: €21,700 per year for non-EU students in 2025–26, plus roughly €15,000 a year living costs

facts.label: Scholarship
facts.value: ITC Excellence Scholarship: about €32,000 of the two-year tuition plus €25,000 towards living costs; you still fund about €17,000 yourself

facts.label: Fee waiver
facts.value: Early Bird: 40 percent tuition waiver for a limited number of unconditionally admitted candidates

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Only a handful of Excellence scholarships per intake; academic record in the top 10 percent of your class is required

facts.label: Pakistani alumni
facts.value: ITC has trained Pakistani staff of SUPARCO, Survey of Pakistan, NESPAK and provincial departments for decades

programmes: Geo-information Science and Earth Observation (M-GEO), specialisations in Natural Resources, Water, Urban Planning, Disaster Risk, Geoinformatics, Earth Sciences
Spatial Engineering (MSc)
details: ITC is a faculty of the University of Twente and the single most GIS-focused graduate school you can apply to. Its M-GEO programme lets you pick a specialisation after a common first quarter, so a geoinformatics graduate from Arid can go into water resources, natural resources, urban planning, disaster risk or earth sciences without changing degree.

Funding is partial. The ITC Excellence Scholarship covers most of the tuition and a share of living costs, but admitted students must prove the remaining amount (around €17,000) before the 1 May payment deadline. The general University of Twente Scholarship does not apply to ITC programmes. The Early Bird 40 percent waiver is a separate route for early, unconditional admits.

Apply for admission first, then for the scholarship in a separate procedure. Strong IELTS (6.5 overall), a bachelor's thesis you can talk about and a clear specialisation choice matter more than the motivation letter.

title: Copernicus Master in Digital Earth (Erasmus Mundus Joint Master)
provider: University of Salzburg with Palacký University Olomouc and Université Bretagne Sud
description: EU-funded joint master's in Earth observation and geoinformatics. Scholarship holders get €1,400 a month for two years plus a full fee waiver.
deadline: 2 November 2026 to 22 January 2027 for the 2027 intake

facts.label: Consortium
facts.value: University of Salzburg (Z_GIS) leads; second year in Olomouc (Geovisualisation and Geocommunication) or Vannes, Bretagne Sud (Geodata Science)

facts.label: Level and length
facts.value: Erasmus Mundus Joint MSc, two years, 120 ECTS, English

facts.label: Scholarship
facts.value: €1,400 per month for 24 months, participation costs waived; self-funded places also offered

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Only the best-ranked applicants receive a scholarship; several hundred apply each year for a small number of funded places

facts.label: Rule
facts.value: You cannot hold a second Erasmus Mundus scholarship if you already had one

programmes: Copernicus Master in Digital Earth
details: The Copernicus Master in Digital Earth is the Erasmus Mundus programme closest to what the institute teaches: satellite Earth observation, spatial analysis and geodata science, built around the EU Copernicus programme. The first year is in Salzburg at Z_GIS, one of Europe's best-known GIS research groups; the second year is either in Olomouc for cartography and geovisualisation or in Vannes for data science.

Erasmus Mundus scholarships are the most generous master's funding available to Pakistani students: tuition is waived and the €1,400 monthly allowance covers living, travel and visa costs. Scholarships go strictly by ranking, so a high CGPA, a relevant thesis and a precise statement of why Digital Earth (not GIS in general) beat polished essays.
Applications for non-European candidates open in November and close in late January. Prepare the IELTS or TOEFL and reference letters before the call opens.

title: Master of Science in Geospatial Technologies (Münster, NOVA Lisbon, Jaume I)
provider: Universität Münster, NOVA IMS, Universitat Jaume I
description: Long-running Erasmus Mundus GIS master's. No scholarships for the 2026 intake; EU funding resumes for the 2027–29 edition, so prepare for the next call.
deadline: Scholarship call expected late 2026 for the 2027 intake

facts.label: Consortium
facts.value: First semester in Castellón (Jaume I) or Lisbon (NOVA IMS), then Münster's Institute for Geoinformatics, thesis at any partner

facts.label: Level and length
facts.value: Joint MSc, 18 months, 90 ECTS, English

facts.label: Funding status
facts.value: Erasmus Mundus scholarships (€1,400 a month plus fee waiver) for the editions 2025–27 and 2027–29 onwards; none for 2026–28

facts.label: Ranking
facts.value: Universität Münster and NOVA are in the QS top 400; Münster's ifgi is one of the strongest geoinformatics research institutes in Europe

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Historically about 20 scholarships per funded intake from several hundred applicants

programmes: Master of Science in Geospatial Technologies
details: This programme has been taking students from Pakistan since the early 2010s and its alumni list includes staff of SUPARCO and several Pakistani universities. It is more software and geoinformatics oriented than the Copernicus master's: spatial databases, geospatial programming, geostatistics and a research thesis at Münster's Institute for Geoinformatics.

The official site states that no scholarships are available for the 2026 intake. A new EU grant covers 2026–2032, with funded editions listed from 2027–29, so the next scholarship call should open in late 2026 for a September 2027 start. Self-funded admission is also possible, with non-EU deadlines at the end of May.
Keep this on the list for the 2027 cycle and apply to the Copernicus Master in Digital Earth in the meantime, since the two calls overlap.

title: DAAD EPOS: MSc Photogrammetry and Geoinformatics, HFT Stuttgart
provider: DAAD with Hochschule für Technik Stuttgart
description: Eight full DAAD scholarships a year for this 18-month English-taught master's in photogrammetry, remote sensing and GIS. Needs two years of work experience.
deadline: 15 October each year (scholarship and admission together)

facts.label: Scholarships
facts.value: 8 full EPOS scholarships per intake, confirmed by DAAD until at least 2029

facts.label: Stipend
facts.value: €992 a month, health insurance, travel allowance, rent subsidy where applicable; no tuition (about €192 semester contribution)

facts.label: Level and length
facts.value: MSc, 3 semesters (18 months), starts winter semester, English

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Bachelor's with above-average grades, at least two years of relevant professional experience, last degree no older than six years

facts.label: Institution
facts.value: HFT Stuttgart is a university of applied sciences; it is not in QS, but the programme has run since 1996 and is the longest-standing DAAD-funded geomatics master's

programmes: Photogrammetry and Geoinformatics (MSc)
details: EPOS (Development-Related Postgraduate Courses) is DAAD's scholarship scheme for professionals from developing countries. This HFT Stuttgart master's is the course in the scheme that matches a geoinformatics degree most closely: digital photogrammetry, laser scanning, remote sensing, spatial databases and web GIS, with a thesis often done with German industry or the German Aerospace Center.

The two years of work experience is a hard requirement, so this suits graduates who have worked at SUPARCO, a provincial GIS cell, NESPAK or a survey firm. Applications go to the university, which forwards a shortlist to DAAD; one application covers both admission and the scholarship.
Since the stipend is paid directly to you and tuition is waived, this is a genuinely full scholarship. Competition is lower than for Erasmus Mundus because of the work-experience filter.

links.label: HFT Stuttgart geomatics news on EPOS

title: DAAD EPOS: other development-related master's in Germany
description: Around 40 funded master's courses for professionals with two years of experience. Several take geoinformatics graduates: water, environmental risk, land management and agriculture.
deadline: August to October, set by each course

facts.label: Stipend

facts.label: Eligibility

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Each course awards roughly 5 to 15 scholarships a year; acceptance is far better than open scholarships because of the experience filter

facts.label: Apply

Hydro Science and Engineering, TU Dresden
Integrated Water Resources Management, TH Köln
Infrastructure Planning, University of Stuttgart
Agricultural Sciences and Resource Management in the Tropics and Subtropics (ARTS), University of Bonn
Land Management and Land Tenure, TU Munich
details: The EPOS brochure lists every funded course with its deadline and contact. Apart from the Stuttgart photogrammetry master's, the courses above regularly admit GIS and remote sensing graduates because they need people who can handle spatial data for floods, water, land and risk.

Pick one or two courses whose thesis topics you can argue from your own work experience. Each course has its own application date, usually between August and October, for a start the following autumn.
Note that the professional experience must be from after your bachelor's, and it must be relevant to the course; internships during study do not count.

title: Fulbright Degree Programme for Pakistan (master's and PhD in the United States)
description: The largest Fulbright programme in the world. Geography, environmental science, urban planning and remote sensing are eligible. About 85 awards in the 2026 cycle.
deadline: Opens February, closes 1 April for the following year's intake

facts.label: Awards
facts.value: 2026 cycle: 85 awards (71 master's, 14 PhD) from roughly 900 applications, about 1 in 10

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: Full tuition, monthly stipend, airfare, health insurance, books; placement at a US university chosen by the Institute of International Education

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: 16 years of education, GRE General (check the current call), Pakistani citizen; PhD applicants sign an HEC bond to return

facts.label: Continuity
facts.value: Fulbright–HEC partnership renewed for financial years 2026–27 to 2031–32

facts.label: Typical placements
facts.value: Clark University, Penn State, University of Maryland (GRAS Remote Sensing top 10 in 2024), University of Arizona, Boston University, Texas A&M

programmes: Any master's or PhD except clinical medicine; relevant fields include Geography, GIS, Remote Sensing, Environmental Science, Urban and Regional Planning, Natural Resources
details: USEFP runs Fulbright for Pakistan and has placed geoinformatics graduates in geography and environmental departments across the United States. You do not choose the university yourself: you list preferences and the programme places you based on your record and field.

The 2025 funding freeze in Washington disrupted stipends for scholars already in the US, but USEFP continued the cycle and the 2026 awards were announced. The 2027 cycle closed on 1 April 2026; expect the next application window to open in February 2027.

Prepare the GRE early, since scores are part of the competition, and write the study objective around a concrete problem in Pakistan (floods, urban growth, crop monitoring) that your degree will address.

title: Chevening Scholarships for one-year master's in the United Kingdom
provider: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
description: Fully funded one-year master's at any UK university for professionals with two years of experience. The UK has more GIS and Earth observation master's than any other country.
deadline: Applications open early August and close in early October

facts.label: Awards
facts.value: About 1,500 scholarships worldwide each year; Pakistan is consistently one of the largest cohorts, typically several dozen scholars

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Roughly 2 to 3 percent of applicants worldwide are selected

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: Full tuition, monthly living allowance, return flights, visa and one-off arrival allowance

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Bachelor's degree, at least two years (2,800 hours) of work experience, must return to Pakistan for two years afterwards

facts.label: Rankings
facts.value: UCL (QS 2027 top 10) and Edinburgh (QS top 40) both run GIS and Earth observation master's that Chevening funds

programmes: MSc Geospatial Sciences, UCL
MSc Earth Observation and Geoinformation Management, University of Edinburgh
MSc Geographical Information Science, University of Leeds
MSc Applied GIS and Remote Sensing, University of Southampton
MSc Geographical Information Science, University of Leicester
MSc Geospatial and Mapping Sciences, University of Glasgow
MSc Remote Sensing and GIS, Aberystwyth University
details: Chevening is the most flexible UK route because you choose three courses yourself and the scholarship follows you. One-year master's keep the opportunity cost low, and the UK has strong Earth observation groups at Edinburgh, Leicester, UCL and Southampton.

Selection weighs leadership, networking and a plan to use the degree back in Pakistan. Four short essays and an interview at the British High Commission decide it. Applicants from government departments, NGOs and the private sector all compete in the same pool.
Apply for the course admissions in parallel; you must hold an unconditional offer from one of your three choices by the summer deadline.

title: Commonwealth Master's and PhD Scholarships (nominated by HEC)
provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
description: Fully funded UK master's and PhD under six development themes. Pakistan's nominations go through HEC: 26 master's and 30 PhD for 2027–28.
deadline: Mid-October on both the HEC and CSC portals

facts.label: Nominations
facts.value: 26 master's and 30 general PhD nominations for Pakistan in the 2027–28 cycle

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: Tuition, monthly stipend (about £1,400, higher in London), return airfare, thesis grant, warm clothing allowance

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Pakistani or AJK national, first-class or 60 percent undergraduate degree, HAT score of at least 60; cannot afford to study in the UK without the award

facts.label: Themes
facts.value: Science and technology for development; strengthening resilience and response to crises; access, inclusion and opportunity; and three others

facts.label: Process
facts.value: Apply twice: on CSC Central and on the HEC scholarship portal; HEC nominates in December, results in July

programmes: Any taught master's or PhD at a UK university under the CSC themes, for example GIS, Earth observation, water and environmental management, disaster risk reduction
details: The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission does not accept direct applications from Pakistan; HEC is the nominating agency and filters by merit and HAT score before the Commission makes the final decision. That makes the HEC stage the real competition.

Frame your application around a development theme. A remote sensing master's for flood early warning fits 'resilience and response to crises'; a GIS degree for land administration fits 'science and technology for development'.
The 2027–28 round closed on 20 October 2026. The next call is expected in August or September 2027.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (HEC Type A and direct Type B)
description: Master's and PhD at Chinese universities with the strongest remote sensing groups in the world, including Wuhan University, ranked first in Remote Sensing for nine consecutive years.
deadline: HEC portal early January; universities' own Type B calls from January to April

facts.label: HEC quota
facts.value: 75 seats in 2026–27: 35 bachelor's, 25 master's, 15 PhD; Type B (direct to universities) adds many more

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: Tuition waived, university dormitory, medical insurance, stipend CNY 3,000 a month for master's and CNY 3,500 for PhD

facts.label: Ranking
facts.value: Wuhan University =165 in QS 2027 and number one worldwide in ShanghaiRanking Remote Sensing 2026 for the ninth year; Tongji, Beijing Normal, Tsinghua and Beijing Institute of Technology also in the Remote Sensing top 10

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Under 35 for master's, under 40 for PhD; 16-year degree; HAT 50 percent for the HEC route

facts.label: Process

programmes: Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, LIESMARS, Wuhan University
Cartography and GIS, Beijing Normal University
Remote Sensing, Aerospace Information Research Institute, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
Surveying and Mapping, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan)
Geomatics, Tongji University
details: China is the single largest destination for Arid geoinformatics graduates going abroad. Its universities dominate the remote sensing subject rankings, laboratories have their own satellites and data, and the funding covers everything except flights.

Type A goes through HEC with a quota of 25 master's and 15 PhD seats; Type B is applied for directly with the university and is where most Pakistani students actually get in, because every major university has its own CSC quota. Contact a supervisor first: a professor's acceptance letter is what moves a Type B application.
Many programmes for international students are in English, but a year of Chinese is sometimes added. Check the language of instruction before you accept.

title: CAS-ANSO Scholarship and ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship, Chinese Academy of Sciences
provider: Chinese Academy of Sciences with ANSO, TWAS and UNESCO
description: The successor of the CAS-TWAS President's Fellowship. Hundreds of funded master's and PhD places a year at CAS institutes including the Aerospace Information Research Institute; the TWAS/UNESCO track adds 40 PhD places for developing countries.
deadline: 31 January each year on the UCAS or USTC admission system

facts.label: Places
facts.value: CAS-ANSO Scholarship: 100 to 200 master's and 300 PhD a year at UCAS, USTC and CAS institutes; ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO track: up to 40 PhD, 10 reserved for climate research

facts.label: Stipend
facts.value: PhD CNY 6,000 a month rising to CNY 7,000 after the qualifying exam (TWAS/UNESCO track); master's lower; tuition, insurance and accommodation covered; up to 48 months for PhD

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Master's degree for PhD, 35 or younger; bachelor's for master's, 30 or younger; from a developing country; not already studying in China

facts.label: Process
facts.value: Apply in the UCAS or USTC international admission system (not both), choose CAS-ANSO Scholarship and tick the TWAS/UNESCO box; a CAS supervisor must accept you first

facts.label: Host institutes
facts.value: Aerospace Information Research Institute (AIR), Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research, Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment, Northwest Institute of Eco-Environment and Resources

programmes: Master's or PhD through the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences at any CAS institute
details: CAS institutes are research organisations rather than teaching universities, so a scholarship here is closer to a paid research job: you join a lab, publish and defend. The Aerospace Information Research Institute in Beijing is one of the largest remote sensing labs in the world, and Pakistani students are a large cohort there.

The old CAS-TWAS President's Fellowship was folded into the ANSO scheme in 2022; third-party sites still advertise it under the old name with the old 31 March deadline. The current deadline is 31 January and the application lives in the UCAS admission system.
You must secure a supervisor before applying. Write to professors in November with a short proposal that cites their papers; the institute then endorses your application.

links.label: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences international admissions

title: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme
provider: Research Grants Council of Hong Kong
description: 400 fellowships for 2027–28 with HK$344,400 a year for three years. PolyU's Land Surveying and Geo-Informatics department and HKU Geography are top-ranked in remote sensing.

facts.label: Fellowships
facts.value: 400 for the 2027–28 academic year

facts.label: Stipend
facts.value: HK$344,400 a year (about US$44,000) plus HK$14,400 conference and travel allowance, for up to three years; universities often top up later years

facts.label: Ranking
facts.value: Hong Kong Polytechnic University 50 in QS 2027; HKU Geography 14th worldwide in ShanghaiRanking Remote Sensing 2026

details: This is the best-paid PhD route in Asia and one of the best anywhere. The stipend is set by the Research Grants Council and does not depend on the supervisor's grant, which removes the usual uncertainty.

PolyU's LSGI department is unusual in combining geodesy, photogrammetry, remote sensing and GIS under one roof, with its own satellite positioning and lidar labs. HKU and CUHK geography departments are strong on urban remote sensing and climate.
A supervisor's support is essential. Email potential supervisors in September with a proposal; the university's own deadline for the fellowship is usually the same 1 December date.

links.label: Department of Land Surveying and Geo-Informatics, PolyU

title: KAUST Fellowship for MS and PhD, Saudi Arabia
provider: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

facts.label: Funding

facts.label: Ranking

MS and PhD in Environmental Science and Engineering
details: KAUST is a research university on the Red Sea with resources few places can match: its own supercomputer, a hydrology and land-observation group that uses drones, satellites and field sensors, and faculty recruited from top US and European departments.
Because the fellowship is automatic, admission is the whole game. Applications are reviewed by faculty, so identify a professor whose work matches your thesis and mention them in the statement.
Pakistani students form one of the larger nationalities on campus. Life is on a closed campus, which some find isolating; visit the student stories before deciding.

details: Stipendium Hungaricum has the largest seat count of any bilateral scholarship for Pakistan, and HEC runs the nomination. The master's stipend is modest by European standards (HUF 43,700 is roughly PKR 35,000), but tuition and housing are covered and Budapest is cheaper than western Europe.

ELTE's Department of Cartography and Geoinformatics runs an English-language MSc that trains in map design, web mapping and GIS programming; it also co-ordinates the Erasmus Mundus cartography master's. Debrecen and Szeged take GIS students into geography programmes.
The round for 2026–27 closed in January 2026. Expect the 2027–28 call in November 2026 with a mid-January deadline; HAT must be sat before you apply.

Results are announced in early August; the Turkish language year starts in September.

Japanese laboratories value a clear research plan over grades. Chiba's CEReS and Tokyo's CSIS have hosted several Pakistani students in remote sensing.

The 2026 Embassy deadline was 25 February. Watch the Embassy of Korea in Islamabad notice board from early February 2027.

provider: Campus France for the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
description: €1,200 a month for master's students nominated by a French university. Toulouse's SIGMA and Strasbourg's Earth observation master's are the geomatics programmes to target.

cost: Stipend; tuition set by the university

facts.label: Allowance
facts.value: €1,200 a month for master's (up to 24 months), about €2,000 for PhD (12 months); international travel, insurance and housing help

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Under 29 for master's, under 35 for PhD; not already studying in France; nominated by the French institution, you cannot apply alone

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Around 350 to 400 master's awards a year worldwide; priority to engineering, science and sustainable development

facts.label: Tuition
facts.value: Not covered by Eiffel; public universities charge about €3,900 a year to non-EU master's students, often waived for Eiffel laureates

facts.label: Language
facts.value: Several geomatics master's are French-taught; check each programme

programmes: Master SIGMA (Science de l'Information Géographique pour la Maîtrise de l'Aménagement), Université Toulouse III and ENSAT
Master Observation de la Terre et Géomatique, Université de Strasbourg
Master Géomatique, Université Paris 1 and ENSG (École nationale des sciences géographiques)
Master Earth and Planetary Sciences (remote sensing track), Université Paris-Saclay
details: Eiffel is a nomination scholarship. You apply to the French master's in the autumn and ask the programme to put you forward; the university then submits your file to Campus France by early January. Results arrive in April.

France's strength is Earth observation science: CNES, the French space agency, co-funds many labs, and Toulouse is Europe's space capital. SIGMA is the best-known applied GIS master's, taught mainly in French with some English.
The allowance does not cover tuition, but most universities waive fees for Eiffel laureates. Budget for the French language requirement in the programmes that need it.

title: MSc Geoinformatics Engineering with merit scholarships, Politecnico di Milano
description: English-taught geoinformatics master's at Italy's top university (QS 2027 =87). Platinum scholarships pay €10,000 a year plus a tuition waiver; the regional DSU grant adds housing and meals for low-income students.
deadline: Early Bird application 1 October to 1 December for the next academic year

facts.label: Ranking
facts.value: Politecnico di Milano =87 in QS 2027 (98 in 2026, the first Italian university in the top 100)

facts.label: Scholarships
facts.value: Platinum €10,000 a year plus tuition waiver; Gold €8,000 plus waiver; Silver tuition waiver only; renewable with credit thresholds

facts.label: DSU grant
facts.value: Regional right-to-study grant for low-income students: cash, free dormitory and canteen; apply after admission with income documents

facts.label: Tuition
facts.value: About €3,900 a year for non-EU students without a waiver

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Scholarships are decided on the admission ranking; a CGPA above 3.5 and a good GRE or strong transcript matter

programmes: Geoinformatics Engineering (Laurea Magistrale), Milan Leonardo campus
details: Polimi's geoinformatics master's comes from its geodesy and photogrammetry school and covers GNSS, geostatistics, image analysis, spatial databases and web GIS, with a strong computing core. It is taught fully in English.

Apply in the Early Bird window (fee paid between 1 October and 1 December) to be considered for merit scholarships; the scholarship form is separate but has no fee. Later applicants can still be admitted but miss the merit round.
Milan is expensive, so the DSU grant matters: students whose family income falls within the regional thresholds get cash, housing and meals regardless of merit scholarships.

title: MSc GIS and Remote Sensing with the Lund University Global Scholarship
description: Two-year master's at a QS top-75 university. The Global Scholarship covers 25 to 100 percent of tuition for top non-EU applicants; living costs are your own.
deadline: Programme application mid-January; scholarship early February

facts.label: Ranking
facts.value: Lund University 71 in QS 2027

facts.label: Tuition
facts.value: SEK 370,000 for the whole programme (about €33,000); the online GIS master's (NAGIV) is SEK 290,000

facts.label: Scholarship
facts.value: Lund University Global Scholarship: 25, 50, 75 or 100 percent of tuition; 110 awarded in 2026 from SEK 26 million; no living allowance

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Non-EU fee-paying applicants with Lund as first choice on universityadmissions.se; 600-word motivation

facts.label: Note
facts.value: Pakistan is not on the 2026 list for the Swedish Institute scholarship, so this is the main funding route to Sweden

programmes: GIS and Remote Sensing, Master Programme (NAGIS)
Geographical Information Science, Master's Programme, distance learning (NAGIV)
details: Lund's physical geography department runs one of Europe's oldest GIS and remote sensing master's, with courses in programming for GIS, satellite remote sensing and ecosystem modelling. The department is also behind the long-running distance GIS master's, which can be studied from Pakistan.
The Global Scholarship is tuition only. With a full waiver, you still need roughly SEK 10,000 a month for living costs, which the Swedish Migration Agency requires you to show.
Apply on universityadmissions.se by mid-January with Lund as first choice, then submit the scholarship motivation in the February window.

title: Remote Sensing and GIS at the Asian Institute of Technology, with AIT scholarships
description: Asia's oldest dedicated RS and GIS master's. AIT gives partial to full tuition scholarships to strong applicants from the region; Pakistani students have studied here since the 1980s.
deadline: August intake applications by March to May; January intake by October

facts.label: Institution
facts.value: International postgraduate institute founded 1959; the RS and GIS programme started in 1980 and hosts the GeoInformatics Center

facts.label: Scholarships
facts.value: AIT Fellowships and His Majesty the King's Scholarships cover tuition partly or fully based on CGPA; some add living allowance

facts.label: Tuition
facts.value: Around US$20,000 for the two-year master's before scholarships

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Admission is moderate; full scholarships need a CGPA around 3.5 or higher

facts.label: Language
facts.value: English; IELTS 6.0 or AIT's own test

programmes: Master of Science in Remote Sensing and Geographic Information Systems
PhD in Remote Sensing and GIS
details: AIT is a regional institute rather than a national university, so it does not appear in QS rankings, but its RS and GIS programme is known across Asia and has trained staff of SUPARCO, SPARCENT and Pakistani universities.
The scholarship amount is decided with the admission offer, so there is no separate application. Scholarships scale with your CGPA and the department's budget that term.
Thailand is inexpensive and the campus is residential. It is a sound choice for a professional master's if European funding does not come through.

title: HEC Overseas Scholarships for MS/MPhil leading to PhD (Phase III)
description: HEC's own fully funded route to QS or THE top-200 universities. Climate, environment, agri-tech and digital transformation are among the thematic areas. Batch IV ran in August 2026.
deadline: Batch IV closed 28 August 2026; watch for the next batch

facts.label: Universities
facts.value: Any university in the QS or Times Higher Education top 200 in an eligible field

facts.label: Themes
facts.value: Energy, climate change and environment; agriculture, food security and agri-tech; digital transformation; natural and physical sciences; engineering; and others

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Pakistani or AJK national; CGPA 3.0 or first division; age 35 (40 for public-sector employees); HAT test; PKR 3,000 processing fee

facts.label: Exemption
facts.value: Applicants holding an unconditional admission to a top-200 university may skip the test and interview

facts.label: Obligation
facts.value: Scholars sign a bond to return and serve in Pakistan

programmes: MS leading to PhD, or direct PhD, in the listed thematic areas at a top-200 university
details: This is the only large scholarship where HEC itself pays the full cost at a university of your choosing, so a confirmed admission from a top-200 university is the strongest card you can hold. Edinburgh, Leeds, Wuhan, KU Leuven, Melbourne and many US state universities fall within the list.

Applications are through the HEC e-Services portal, followed by the HEC Aptitude Test and an interview. Batches are announced irregularly, roughly once a year, so set an alert on the HEC announcements page.
Previous HEC MS scholars must complete two years in Pakistan before reapplying.

title: Australian Research Training Program PhD scholarships
description: Tax-free stipend of about AUD 33,000 to 35,000 a year plus fee offset for international PhD students. Curtin, UQ, UNSW, Tasmania and RMIT have strong spatial science groups.
deadline: Usually August to October for the following year; set by each university

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: RTP stipend (about AUD 33,500 a year in 2025, indexed), tuition fee offset and overseas health cover, for 3 to 3.5 years

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: International RTP places are limited; universities rank applicants by publications, thesis and supervisor support

facts.label: Ranking
facts.value: University of Queensland, UNSW and University of Melbourne are in the QS top 40; Curtin's spatial sciences and Tasmania's geography and spatial sciences are well-regarded

facts.label: Process
facts.value: Secure a supervisor, then apply for admission and scholarship together through the university's graduate research office

programmes: PhD, School of Earth and Planetary Sciences (Spatial Sciences), Curtin University
PhD, School of the Environment, University of Queensland
PhD, School of Geography, Planning and Spatial Sciences, University of Tasmania
PhD, Geospatial Science, RMIT University
PhD, Faculty of Science and Engineering, University of New South Wales
details: Australia funds its PhD students through the Research Training Program, which each university allocates. There is no central application: you find a supervisor, agree on a project and apply in the university's scholarship round, usually between August and October for a start the following year.

Australian groups lead in agricultural remote sensing, bushfire and drought monitoring, and lidar and photogrammetry, all directly relevant to Pakistan's problems. Several Arid graduates have taken this route through CSIRO-linked supervisors.
Some universities supplement RTP with their own scholarships, for example Curtin's International Postgraduate Research Scholarship and UQ's Graduate School Scholarship.

title: Funded MSc and PhD in Geomatics Engineering, University of Calgary
provider: Schulich School of Engineering, University of Calgary
description: One of the largest geomatics departments in North America. Thesis-based graduate students receive guaranteed minimum funding from supervisors, teaching assistantships and awards.
deadline: 15 January for September admission with full funding consideration

facts.label: Institution
facts.value: Department of Geomatics Engineering: GNSS, photogrammetry, lidar, remote sensing, GIS and land tenure; roughly 30 faculty

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: Thesis-based MSc and PhD students get a guaranteed minimum stipend (around CAD 20,000 to 26,000 a year) from research grants and teaching assistantships; international tuition is deducted from it

facts.label: Ranking
facts.value: University of Calgary in the QS top 200; the geomatics department is among the best-known in Canada alongside UNB and Laval

facts.label: Process
facts.value: Email a professor with a proposal and CV; applications without a supervisor's interest are rarely funded

programmes: MSc and PhD in Geomatics Engineering
details: Canadian research degrees are paid for by the supervisor's grant, so the application is really a job application to a professor. Calgary's geomatics department has a long record of taking students from Pakistan, several of whom now teach at NUST and UET.
Funding is enough to live on in Calgary if you budget carefully; international tuition is around CAD 12,000 a year and comes out of the stipend package.
Apply by 15 January with IELTS 7.0 (6.5 in each band) and a research statement; GRE is not required.

title: Open Doors Russian Scholarship Project (tuition-free master's and PhD)
provider: Global Universities Association, Russian Ministry of Science and Higher Education
description: Online olympiad whose winners study free at 24 Russian universities. The Earth and Environmental Sciences track covers geography, geoinformatics and remote sensing.
deadline: Registration 20 August to 1 November 2026; second round by 16 November

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: Tuition-free study under the Russian government quota; monthly stipend set by the university (small); accommodation not guaranteed

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Master's track: aged 20 to 33, no prior master's; PhD track: master's degree

facts.label: Selection
facts.value: Stage 1 portfolio, stage 2 proctored 180-minute subject test online; PhD applicants also interview with a supervisor

facts.label: Track
facts.value: Earth and Environmental Sciences for Sustainability; also Urbanism and Civil Engineering

facts.label: Universities
facts.value: 24 including Moscow State, Saint Petersburg State, HSE, ITMO, Tomsk State and Ural Federal

programmes: Master's or PhD in the Earth and Environmental Sciences track at a participating university
details: Open Doors is unusual in that selection is an exam rather than an essay, which suits strong students without work experience. Winners choose a university and programme from the participating list.

The stipend is nominal, so you need savings for living costs, and many programmes are Russian-taught with a preparatory year. Check the language of instruction for the specific programme before you commit.
Registration for the 2026–27 edition closes 1 November 2026, with a second-round registration deadline on 16 November for bachelor's, master's and PhD tracks.

title: Schlumberger Foundation Faculty for the Future (women in STEM, PhD and postdoc)
description: Fellowships of up to US$50,000 a year for women from developing countries doing a PhD or postdoc in science and engineering abroad, on condition they return to teach or research at home.
deadline: September to November each year

facts.label: Award
facts.value: Up to US$50,000 a year for PhD, up to US$40,000 for postdoc, renewable

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Women from developing and emerging countries (Pakistan eligible), admitted to or enrolled in a PhD or postdoc abroad in a STEM field, committed to returning home

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Around 50 new fellows a year worldwide from several hundred applicants

facts.label: Fields
facts.value: Earth sciences, environmental science, geoinformatics and remote sensing qualify

programmes: Any PhD or postdoc abroad; the fellowship is portable
details: Faculty for the Future targets women who will become faculty at universities in their home countries. Pakistani fellows have studied geosciences and environmental science at universities in Europe, Australia and North America.
You need an admission or a current enrolment first; the fellowship then funds the remaining years. Pair it with a partial scholarship such as ITC Excellence or Lund to close the gap.
Applications open in September and close in November for the following academic year.

title: Ernst Mach Grant worldwide: research stays in Austria
description: €1,300 a month for one to nine months of research at an Austrian university, for MS or PhD students and postdocs from any country. A door into Salzburg's Z_GIS and TU Wien's geoinformation group.
deadline: 1 March each year

facts.label: Grant
facts.value: €1,300 a month, accident and health insurance, up to nine months; travel costs sometimes subsidised

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Postgraduate or doctoral students and postdocs under 35 (45 for postdocs) from any country except Austria; invitation letter from an Austrian host

facts.label: Hosts
facts.value: Z_GIS at the University of Salzburg, Department of Geodesy and Geoinformation at TU Wien, BOKU Vienna, TU Graz

facts.label: Note
facts.value: The ASEA-UNINET version of this grant is limited to South-East Asian countries; Pakistan uses the worldwide call

programmes: Research stay of 1 to 9 months as part of an MS thesis, PhD or postdoc
details: This is not a degree scholarship but a paid research visit, which is how many PhD students in Pakistan collect data, co-author papers and build the contact that later turns into a funded PhD or postdoc.
Apply on grants.at with a research plan and a letter from the Austrian host. Z_GIS has hosted Pakistani researchers in object-based image analysis and disaster mapping.
The HEC and the Austrian government also run a joint scholarship from time to time; check HEC announcements.

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master catalogue: other programmes for geo graduates
provider: European Education and Culture Executive Agency
description: Search the official catalogue for water, environment, climate, forestry and urban programmes that take geoinformatics graduates. Every scholarship pays €1,400 a month plus fees.
deadline: Mostly December to February for the following autumn

facts.label: Scholarship
facts.value: €1,400 a month for the whole programme, participation costs waived; the same package across all joint master's

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Each programme funds roughly 10 to 25 students a year; several hundred apply

facts.label: Rule
facts.value: Apply to up to three joint master's per year; one Erasmus Mundus scholarship per lifetime

programmes: Copernicus Master in Digital Earth (Salzburg, Olomouc, Bretagne Sud)
Geospatial Technologies (Münster, NOVA, Jaume I), funded again from the 2027 intake
Cartography M.Sc. (TU Munich, TU Vienna, TU Dresden, Twente), scholarships depend on the current grant
Environmental Sciences, Policy and Management (MESPOM)
Flood Risk Management or water-focused joint master's, check the catalogue
Sustainable Forest and Nature Management (SUFONAMA)
details: The catalogue lists every programme currently funded and links to each consortium's own site, where the application lives. Filter by keyword ('earth', 'environment', 'water', 'urban') since the field labels are broad.
Scholarship decisions are ranked lists per programme. The same application quality that fails at one consortium can win at another with fewer applicants, so use all three of your yearly choices.
Funding is for the programme's whole length; there is no separate travel allowance any more, the monthly amount covers it.

title: End-to-End Google Earth Engine
description: The most complete free Earth Engine course: from the code editor to supervised classification, time series and change detection, with Earth Engine apps at the end.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Self-paced text and video with runnable scripts; also run as a paid live class

facts.label: Time
facts.value: About 30 hours

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Beginner to intermediate; no programming required at the start

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: Free material; certificate only through the paid instructor-led version

details: Ujaval Gandhi's course is the standard introduction to Earth Engine and is updated with every API change. Modules cover cloud masking, Sentinel and Landsat composites, classification and accuracy assessment, time series analysis and exporting results.
Do every exercise rather than just reading. The quiz-style assignments translate directly into final-year project chapters.

title: NASA ARSET applied remote sensing trainings
description: Free live and recorded trainings on floods, drought, air quality, agriculture and land cover using NASA data. Certificates of completion for live sessions.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Webinar series of 3 to 5 sessions, English and Spanish, recordings available

facts.label: Time
facts.value: 4 to 10 hours per training

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Introductory and advanced tracks

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: Certificate of completion for live attendees who finish the homework

details: ARSET trainings are built by NASA scientists around real applications: SAR for flood mapping, MODIS and VIIRS for fire and drought, Landsat and HLS for crops, and GPM for rainfall. Each session comes with step-by-step exercises in QGIS, SNAP or Earth Engine.

ARSET moved from appliedsciences.nasa.gov to NASA Earthdata in July 2025; old links still redirect. The SAR, NISAR and hydrology series are the most useful for Pakistan's flood and water work. Register for live sessions to earn the certificate; the recordings are free any time.

title: Esri MOOCs: Cartography, Spatial Data Science, Imagery in Action and more
description: Six-week free courses with a temporary ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online licence included. A certificate at the end.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Six-week cohorts, two or three runs a year; about 2 to 3 hours a week

facts.label: Courses
facts.value: Cartography., Spatial Data Science: The New Frontier in Analytics, Imagery in Action, Going Places with Spatial Analysis, Do-It-Yourself Geo Apps

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: Esri certificate of completion, recognised on LinkedIn

facts.label: Licence
facts.value: ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online access for the course duration at no cost

details: Esri's MOOCs are the only free way to use the full ArcGIS Pro stack with Esri's own training data. 'Cartography.' is the one every GIS student should take; 'Imagery in Action' covers deep learning on imagery inside ArcGIS Pro.
Cohorts fill quickly. Register a free Esri public account first and watch the schedule page.

links.label: Esri Academy catalogue (many free web courses)

title: Echoes in Space: radar remote sensing (SAR)
description: The reference free course on synthetic aperture radar: physics, Sentinel-1 processing in SNAP, interferometry and polarimetry. Essential for flood and subsidence mapping.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Video lectures, readings and SNAP exercises; self-paced

facts.label: Time
facts.value: About 25 hours

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Intermediate; some remote sensing background helps

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: Certificate of completion on passing the quizzes

details: Radar is the data source that works through monsoon clouds, which is why Sentinel-1 drove most of Pakistan's 2022 flood mapping. This course, run by the German Aerospace Center and ESA on the EO College platform, is the most thorough free introduction.
EO College also hosts 'Hyperspectral: Beyond the Visible', 'Cubes and Clouds' on cloud-native EO, and 'Land in Focus' on land cover and biodiversity.

title: Earth Observation from Space: the Optical View
description: ESA's five-week introduction to optical satellites, from radiation physics to land, ocean and atmosphere applications. Free to study during the run; certificate paid.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Five weeks, 3 hours a week, videos and discussions

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Beginner

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: Paid upgrade (about £40 to £60) for the certificate and permanent access

details: A gentle conceptual course that explains what the sensors measure before any software. Good in first or second year alongside the physics of remote sensing course.
FutureLearn restricts free access to the course run plus two weeks, so finish it in the window or pay for the upgrade.

title: Google Earth Engine official tutorials and guides
description: Google's own tutorials, from the beginner's cookbook to machine learning with TensorFlow and the Python API. The reference you return to after any course.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Written tutorials with code; community tutorials included

facts.label: Level
facts.value: All levels

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: None

details: Pair this with the Spatial Thoughts course. The 'Beginner's Cookbook', 'Introduction to the Python API' and the geemap tutorials cover everything needed for a thesis pipeline.
Earth Engine is free for non-commercial and research use; register a project under the non-commercial tier with your university email.

links.label: Cloud-Based Remote Sensing with Google Earth Engine (free book)

title: GIS, Mapping, and Spatial Analysis Specialization
description: Four courses with ArcGIS Pro covering GIS fundamentals, data, spatial analysis and a capstone. Audit free; certificate about US$49 a month.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Four courses, video and assignments, ArcGIS Pro trial included

facts.label: Time
facts.value: About 60 hours

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Beginner

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: Coursera specialization certificate with the paid plan; financial aid available on each course

details: Don Boyes' specialization is the best-reviewed introductory GIS sequence on Coursera and uses ArcGIS Pro throughout, so it doubles as practice for the Esri certification.
Coursera financial aid is approved for most students from Pakistan who write a short justification; apply per course, about two weeks in advance.

links.label: Geographic Information Systems Specialization, UC Davis (QGIS)
Spatial Data Science and Applications, Yonsei

title: Penn State open courseware in GIS and remote sensing
provider: Penn State College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
description: Full master's-level course material from Penn State's online GIS programme, free to read: GIS programming, remote sensing image analysis, lidar, cartography and spatial databases.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Complete lesson texts, assignments and readings; no instructor

facts.label: Courses
facts.value: GEOG 485 GIS Programming and Software Development, GEOG 480 Exploring Imagery and Elevation Data, GEOG 883 Remote Sensing Image Analysis, GEOG 486 Cartography and Visualization, GEOG 868 Spatial Database Management

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Intermediate to advanced

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: None; the paid Penn State certificate is listed under Certifications

details: These are the actual course pages Penn State uses for its ranked online master's, published openly. GEOG 485 is one of the best introductions to Python for ArcGIS; GEOG 883 is a full object-based image analysis course.
Use them to go deeper than the semester allows, or as structured reading for a thesis method.

title: QGIS Training Manual and A Gentle Introduction to GIS
description: The official QGIS course, with sample data, from the interface to vector analysis, rasters, databases, forestry applications and plugins.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Written modules with downloadable exercise data

facts.label: Time
facts.value: About 40 hours for the full manual

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Beginner to intermediate

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: None; QGIS certified trainers (see Certifications) issue certificates for their own courses

details: The manual is maintained by the QGIS community and matches the current long-term release. It is the text behind most QGIS certified training worldwide.
Spatial Thoughts' 'Advanced QGIS' and 'Python Foundation for Spatial Analysis' are the natural next steps.

title: Automating GIS Processes and Geo-Python
description: Helsinki's open master's course on Python for GIS: GeoPandas, Shapely, rasterio, OSMnx and network analysis. Preceded by Geo-Python for programming basics.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Lessons with Jupyter notebooks and weekly exercises

facts.label: Time
facts.value: About 50 hours across both courses

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Beginner (Geo-Python) to intermediate (AutoGIS)

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: None

details: This is the course most open-source geospatial developers recommend for learning the Python stack properly. Every lesson runs in a browser notebook, so nothing needs to be installed to start.
After AutoGIS, the free books 'Geographic Data Science with Python' and 'Geocomputation with R' take you into modelling.

title: Earth Data Science courses and textbooks
provider: Earth Lab, University of Colorado Boulder
description: Free textbooks and courses on Earth data analytics in Python: Landsat and NAIP processing, lidar, time series, with the data provided.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Online textbook chapters with code and datasets

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Intermediate

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: None (CU Boulder's paid professional certificate uses the same material)

details: Earth Lab's material is the base for CU Boulder's Earth Data Analytics professional certificate, and all of it is open. The lidar and raster chapters are particularly strong.
Good companion to AutoGIS once you are comfortable with Python.

title: ESA SNAP tutorials
description: Official step-by-step tutorials for processing Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3 data in SNAP, including interferometry and ship detection.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: PDF and video tutorials with sample products

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Beginner to advanced

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: None

details: SNAP is the free software ESA built for Sentinel data, and these tutorials are written by the toolbox developers. Start with 'Sentinel-1 flood mapping' and 'Sentinel-2 land cover classification'.
The RUS Copernicus training archive on the same site has recorded webinars with full datasets.

title: UN-SPIDER recommended practices for disaster mapping
provider: UN Office for Outer Space Affairs
description: Step-by-step workflows for flood, drought, landslide and burn mapping with free data and software, written for national disaster agencies.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Written workflows with sample data, QGIS, SNAP and Earth Engine

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Intermediate

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: None

details: These are the workflows NDMA, PDMAs and UN agencies in Pakistan actually use for rapid mapping. The Sentinel-1 flood mapping practice in Earth Engine and the drought monitoring practice are the two to master before applying for a disaster-management GIS job.
Each practice lists the data, the steps and the limitations, which makes them good templates for methodology chapters.

title: LearnOSM: OpenStreetMap mapping and data
description: How to map in OpenStreetMap, use JOSM and field tools, and pull OSM data into QGIS. Relevant for humanitarian GIS jobs and base mapping in Pakistan.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Written guides in several languages

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Beginner

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: None; your OSM contribution history is the credential

details: iMMAP, REACH and UN agencies look for OSM experience in GIS officer postings. Mapping your own district and validating in the HOT Tasking Manager is free evidence of skill.
The guides also cover the Overpass API and QGIS QuickOSM plugin for extracting roads, buildings and amenities.

title: Spatial Thoughts instructor-led classes (paid)
description: Live online cohorts for Earth Engine, Python, QGIS and mapping with graded assignments and a certificate. Fees in Indian rupees; student discounts offered.
cost: Paid, roughly US$100 to 200 per course

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Four to eight weeks, live sessions with recordings, assignments reviewed by instructors

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: Certificate of completion on passing the assignments

facts.label: Courses
facts.value: End-to-End Google Earth Engine, Python Foundation for Spatial Analysis, Mapping and Data Visualization with Python, Advanced QGIS

details: The same free material taught live, with feedback on your code. Worth it if you want the certificate and an instructor looking at your work; otherwise the free versions are complete.
Spatial Thoughts offers discounted or free seats to students and to people from low-income countries; ask before paying.

title: Spatial data science with R (rspatial.org)
description: The terra and raster package author's own tutorials: spatial data in R, remote sensing, species distribution modelling and spatial regression.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Written tutorials with R code and data

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Intermediate

facts.label: Certificate
facts.value: None

details: If your thesis statistics live in R, this is where to learn to keep the rasters there too. The remote sensing chapter covers Landsat classification and NDVI time series in terra.
Pair with 'Geocomputation with R' for sf and tmap.

title: GISP: Certified GIS Professional
description: The main vendor-neutral GIS credential, held by more than 10,000 professionals. Needs an exam plus a portfolio of education, four years of experience and contributions to the profession.
cost: US$250 exam plus US$250 portfolio review

facts.label: Requirements
facts.value: Pass the GISCI Geospatial Core Technical Knowledge Exam, then a portfolio: education points, at least four years of professional experience, and contributions (presentations, volunteering, publications)

facts.label: Exam
facts.value: 150 multiple-choice questions, four hours, at Pearson VUE centres including Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: Exam US$250, portfolio review US$250, renewal every three years US$95 plus continuing-education points

facts.label: Recognition
facts.value: Required or preferred in many US, Canadian and Gulf GIS job postings; recognised by UN agencies

facts.label: Timing
facts.value: You can sit the exam as a student and submit the portfolio after you reach four years of experience; the exam result is valid for six years

details: The GISP exam tests the Geospatial Technology Competency Model: conceptual foundations, cartography, data, analysis, GIS design and professional practice, with no software vendor bias. Sitting it in final year, while the coursework is fresh, is a sensible plan.
Pakistan's job market does not ask for GISP yet, but Gulf consultancies and international organisations do, and it carries weight when competing for remote roles.

title: Esri Technical Certification (ArcGIS Pro, Enterprise, Developer)
description: Esri's own exams at Foundation, Associate and Professional levels for ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Online and developer tracks. The credential employers in Pakistan and the Gulf recognise most.

facts.label: Exams
facts.value: ArcGIS Pro Foundation, Associate and Professional; ArcGIS Enterprise Administration Associate and Professional; ArcGIS Online Administration; ArcGIS Developer Associate; Image Analyst and Utility Network specialties

facts.label: Format
facts.value: About 90 multiple-choice questions, two hours, online proctored or Pearson VUE

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: US$250 per exam; Esri occasionally discounts for students and at the User Conference

facts.label: Validity
facts.value: Tied to a product version; Esri lists which versions are current

facts.label: Preparation
facts.value: Free Esri Academy web courses and the MOOCs cover most of the Associate syllabus

details: ArcGIS Pro Associate is the sensible first target: it certifies day-to-day editing, analysis and map production. The Professional exam adds geoprocessing design, data management and automation with ModelBuilder and Python.
Pakistani employers using ArcGIS (SUPARCO, Urban Unit, NESPAK, oil and gas, utilities) and Gulf consultancies list Esri certification as a plus. Pay in US dollars; an international card is needed.

title: ASPRS Certified Photogrammetrist, Mapping Scientist and Technologist
provider: American Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
description: The oldest geospatial certification (since 1975) in photogrammetry, remote sensing, GIS/LIS, lidar and UAS. Technologist level is open with three years' experience; full certification needs six.

facts.label: Tracks
facts.value: Certified Photogrammetrist; Certified Mapping Scientist in Remote Sensing, GIS/LIS, Lidar or UAS; Certified Technologist in each (entry level)

facts.label: Requirements
facts.value: Technologist: three years of experience; full certification: six years with references; written exam in all cases

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: Application fee around US$250 (member) and exam fee; recertification every five years

facts.label: Recognition
facts.value: Standard in US and Canadian survey and mapping contracts; valued by drone and lidar companies

details: ASPRS certification is for people who produce measured products: orthophotos, DEMs, lidar classifications, drone surveys. If you are heading into photogrammetry or UAS mapping, the Technologist exam is attainable within three years of graduation.
Exams can be proctored remotely for international candidates; contact ASPRS certification staff to arrange it.

title: USGIF Certified GEOINT Professional (CGP)
description: Three exams, in GIS and analysis tools, remote sensing and imagery analysis, and geospatial data management, for geospatial intelligence analysts. Also a general CGP-G exam.

facts.label: Exams
facts.value: CGP-G (general), CGP-GA (GIS and analysis tools), CGP-RS (remote sensing and imagery analysis), CGP-GD (geospatial data management)

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Computer-based, about 100 questions; no experience requirement for sitting, a degree in a geospatial field recommended

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: Roughly US$225 to 300 per exam, discounts for USGIF members and students

facts.label: Recognition
facts.value: Mainly US defence and intelligence contractors; useful evidence of imagery-analysis skill for international applications

details: The CGP-RS exam is the most relevant to a remote sensing graduate: sensor types, image interpretation, change detection, SAR and multispectral analysis. It is one of the few certifications that test remote sensing directly rather than GIS software.
Some exams require a US citizenship check for the GEOINT-specific tracks; check eligibility for international candidates before paying.

title: UNIGIS professional and MSc in Geographical Information Science (distance)
description: Part-time distance diploma and MSc from Salzburg's Z_GIS and partner universities, studied from Pakistan while working. Paid, with occasional partial waivers.
cost: UNIGIS professional about €5,000; MSc about €10,000 to 12,000

facts.label: Levels
facts.value: UNIGIS professional (postgraduate diploma, 18 months, 60 ECTS) and MSc GIS (two to three years, 120 ECTS), both part-time online

facts.label: Institution
facts.value: University of Salzburg (Z_GIS), with the Erasmus Mundus Copernicus master's run by the same department; UNIGIS partners in Latin America, Europe and Asia

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: Fees paid per module; Salzburg's professional programme is roughly €5,000, the MSc roughly €10,000 to 12,000; small scholarships announced on the site

facts.label: Recognition
facts.value: A full Austrian university degree; accepted for PhD admission across Europe

details: UNIGIS has been running since 1990 and is the most established way to earn a European GIS master's without leaving your job. Modules cover data modelling, spatial analysis, remote sensing, geovisualisation, web GIS and a thesis.
The cost is high for Pakistan but far below moving abroad. Employers such as NGOs sometimes co-fund it.

title: Penn State online Postbaccalaureate Certificate in GIS
description: Four graduate courses (12 credits) from the top-ranked US online GIS programme, counting towards the Penn State MGIS. Paid, around US$12,000.

facts.label: Content
facts.value: GIS fundamentals, cartography and visualization, GIS programming, plus one elective such as remote sensing, lidar or spatial databases

facts.label: Time
facts.value: About 12 to 18 months part-time

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: Roughly US$1,000 per credit for 12 credits; no scholarships for international students

facts.label: Recognition
facts.value: Penn State's online GIS programme is consistently ranked first among US online master's; credits transfer to the MGIS

details: The same lessons are published free in the open courseware listed under Courses; the certificate pays for grading, instructors and the Penn State transcript. It makes sense for professionals whose employer pays or who plan to continue into the MGIS.
Admission needs a bachelor's with a 3.0 GPA and TOEFL or IELTS.

title: QGIS certified training certificates
description: QGIS.org endorses training organisations whose courses issue official QGIS certificates, with a small fee that funds the project. Several trainers run online cohorts open to Pakistan.
cost: Course fee set by the trainer, typically US$100 to 500; €20 per certificate to QGIS.org

facts.label: How it works
facts.value: Complete a course at a QGIS certified organisation; the certificate is issued through QGIS.org's registry and is verifiable online

facts.label: Providers
facts.value: Kartoza (South Africa), Lutra Consulting (UK), OPENGIS.ch (Switzerland), Geocodis and others run remote courses

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: Set by each provider; the certificate fee is a donation to QGIS development

facts.label: Recognition
facts.value: The only official credential tied to QGIS; useful for NGO and UN postings that run on open-source software

details: There is no QGIS exam. The certificate attests that you took a course from an organisation vetted by QGIS.org. Choose a provider whose course syllabus matches the job you want: Kartoza's courses for general GIS, Lutra for QGIS and Mergin Maps field work.
Combine it with public work: plugins, contributions to the QGIS documentation or translated training material are visible evidence.

title: Chartered Geographer (GIS), Royal Geographical Society
description: The UK's professional charter for geographers, with a GIS specialism. Requires a geography-related degree and six years of experience (less with a master's). Recognised across the Commonwealth.
cost: About £100 application; annual RGS fellowship fee

facts.label: Requirements
facts.value: A relevant degree plus six years of professional experience (reduced for postgraduate degrees), a professional report and a referee; continuing professional development each year

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: Application around £100 plus Fellowship of the RGS (about £130 a year)

facts.label: Recognition
facts.value: Chartered status protected by Royal Charter; used by UK and Commonwealth consultancies and government geospatial posts

facts.label: Suits
facts.value: Alumni working in the UK, Gulf or for British consultancies, or planning a Chevening route

details: CGeog (GIS) is a career-stage credential rather than an exam: it proves sustained professional practice and ethics. Start logging continuing professional development early if you want it later.
Membership of the RGS also gives access to the journal archive and the Geographical Information Science Research UK community.

deadline: Rolling

description: Sample entry. Summer internship for third-year students; replace with a live posting.
